chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person in ihram who looked at his wife and emitted semen or pre-seminal fluid while he was in ihram. He said: 'There is no penalty upon him.' The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as him looking at her without lust, so no penalty was incumbent upon him. And the penalty is only incumbent if he looked with lust, causing emission, according to what was detailed in the first report.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٍ: Person in ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a person in ihram who looks at their wife?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing that the liability for kaffarah in ihram depends on the presence of lust (shahwah) rather than the mere act of looking. The scholar explains that if the gaze was devoid of lust, no penalty is due even if seminal fluid was emitted, whereas kaffarah is only incurred if the looking was accompanied by lust leading to emission.
